forget/one: The delta rule edits one key per token. That is precise, but when a text moves on to a new topic, every old pair goes stale, and the rule can only clear them one key at a time.
forget/decay: A selective state space model forgets the other way: each token multiplies the whole state by a decay, a, made from the token itself, so one token can fade the whole memory at once.
forget/mamba2: Its 2024 successor, Mamba2, by Tree Dao and Albert Gu, can be written as linear attention with that decay: S becomes a times S, plus v k transpose.
forget/blunt: But the decay is blunt: it fades every pair alike. With a at a half, both values halve. To forget one stale pair, it must fade them all.
gate/both: Gated DeltaNet does both. Each token first fades the whole state by alpha, a number between zero and one, made from the token the way a selective state space model makes its decay.
gate/gate: alpha is called a gate: like an LSTM's forget gate, it lets through a share of the memory, set by the input.
gate/delta: Then it applies the delta rule to the faded state: read what it now holds for the key, and write the difference, times beta.
gate/rule: Together: S gets alpha S, plus beta, times v minus alpha S k, times k transpose.
gate/ends: At alpha near zero, the old memory is wiped, and the token starts it afresh. At alpha of one, nothing fades, and it is the delta rule again.
run/start: Run one step. Key one, zero reads two, three, and key zero, one reads one, four. A token arrives with alpha of a half, beta of one, key one, zero and value four, one.
run/fade: First the fade: everything halves. Key one, zero now reads one, one and a half.
run/diff: Its difference from the new value, four, one, is three, minus a half.
run/write: Written along the key, it makes key one, zero read exactly four, one.
run/k2: Key zero, one was not written: it reads half of one, four, which is a half, two. The new pair is exact, and the rest has faded by alpha.
results/paper: Songlin Yang, Jan Kautz and Ali Hatamizadeh, at MIT and en vidia, proposed this gated delta rule in 2024. They trained models of one point three billion parameters on a hundred billion tokens to compare.
results/needle: One test hid a single fact, a key with its value, in a long text, and asked for it at the end: a needle in a haystack.
results/repeat: In filler that repeats, the delta rule kept the needle at every length, while Mamba2's decay faded it past two thousand tokens.
results/essay: Hidden in real essays, where every sentence might matter, plain DeltaNet fell behind past a thousand tokens: with nothing cleared, its pairs collided. The gated models held up longer.
results/best: Across language modelling, reasoning and recall, Gated DeltaNet beat both Mamba2 and DeltaNet, and trained about as fast as DeltaNet.
